title: Injectivity of the canonical special-chart map
statement: With prepared data d [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-lift-preparation], maps c and cmod as in [def-weil-pbc-popescu-special-chart-map], and c sending epsilon(X_i) to the original quotient generator x_i for every i, the canonical special-chart map [def-weil-pbc-popescu-special-chart-map] is injective for every k. Equivalently, its kernel is zero; no surjectivity or algebra-equivalence assertion is included.

source.place: Stacks Project, Tag 07CP, displayed calculation modulo pi and comparison of chart coefficients; read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07CP on 2026-10-13.

proof.text: Use the descended C0-algebra substitution from the unlocalized lifting quotient. hcmod identifies the element t to be inverted with the image of a0. Algebra compatibility identifies its substitution with the coefficient algebra map, whose value at a0 is a unit in the localized polynomial ring. Extend the substitution to G on the localized lifting quotient using Away.liftAlgHom.

The composite G with the canonical chart map fixes each free polynomial variable by the substitution values and the localization lift equation. Its restriction to localized coefficients equals C: localization ringHom_ext reduces this to the base C0, where both algebra homomorphisms commute with scalar maps. MvPolynomial.ringHom_ext gives the identity composite. Function.LeftInverse.injective finishes.

proof_origin.place: M1 reduction of the Tag 07CP argument: descent separated from localization and extensionality
